Exponential growth dominates polynomial growth, so C(x) -> infinity much faster than R(x). Therefore the ratio R(x)/C(x) behaves like (3x^8)/(2^x), which tends to 0 as x -> infinity.

R(x)=3x^8+4x^2 is a degree-8 polynomial, so R(x) ~ 3x^8 and R(x) -> infinity. C(x)=2^x-x^3: exponential 2^x dominates any polynomial x^3, so C(x) -> infinity and is eventually positive. For large x, R(x) <= 4x^8 while C(x) >= (1/2)2^x, say, so R/C <= 8x^8/2^x. Since x^8/2^x -> 0 by repeated exponential domination, lim R/C = 0.
